rows.acip: BDAG 'DZIN GNYIS LTA BU'I YID SHES KYI SHES PA DE JI LTAR 'GRUB PA NI, TSIG GSAL LAS, GAL TE MTSAN GZHI'AM RANG GI MTSAN NYID DAM SPYI'I MTSAN NYID KYANG RUNG STE, 'JIG RTEN NA YOD NA NI THAMS CAD MNGON SUM DU DMIGS PAR BYA BA YIN PA'I PHYIR LKOG TU MA GYUR BA YIN TE, DE'I PHYIR DE'I YUL CAN GYI RNAM PAR SHES PA DANG LHAN CIG TU MNGON SUM NYID DU RNAM PAR BZHAG GO ,ZHES GSUNGS PA 'DIS SHES PAR BYA'O,,
rows.wylie: bdag 'dzin gnyis lta bu'i yid shes kyi shes pa de ji ltar 'grub pa ni, tshig gsal las, gal te mtshan gzhi'am rang gi mtshan nyid dam spyi'i mtshan nyid kyang rung ste, 'jig rten na yod na ni thams cad mngon sum du dmigs par bya ba yin pa'i phyir lkog tu ma gyur ba yin te, de'i phyir de'i yul can gyi rnam par shes pa dang lhan cig tu mngon sum nyid du rnam par bzhag go ,zhes gsungs pa 'dis shes par bya'o
rows.english: How is it then that we establish perceptions of the consciousness of the thought for things like the two forms of the tendency to believe in some kind of self-existence? The answer to this question can be understood from the following description found in A Clarification of the Verses— It doesn't matter whether we're talking about a defining occurrence of something; or the definition of something; or the general characteristics of the thing. When things are said to exist in the everyday world, then all of them are objects which can be observed directly. As such, they are not what we would call “recondite.” And for this reason, they are established exclusively as being direct, part & parcel with the relevant subject state of awareness.

rows.acip: DES NA 'DIS MTSON PAR BYED PA'I MTSAN NYID DANG, 'DI MTSON PAR BYA BA'I MTSAN GZHI THAMS CAD MNGON SUM DU DMIGS PAR BYA BAR BSHAD PA NI, TSAD MA BZHIR BYAS PA'I MNGON SUM TSAD MA NGOS 'DZIN PA'I SKABS YIN PA'I PHYIR, THAMS CAD MKHYEN PAS MNGON SUM DU DMIGS PAR STON PA YANG MIN LA,
rows.wylie: des na 'dis mtshon par byed pa'i mtshan nyid dang, 'di mtshon par bya ba'i mtshan gzhi thams cad mngon sum du dmigs par bya bar bshad pa ni, tshad ma bzhir byas pa'i mngon sum tshad ma ngos 'dzin pa'i skabs yin pa'i phyir, thams cad mkhyen pas mngon sum du dmigs par ston pa yang min la
rows.english: And so let's take a look at the definition which acts to define the thing; and the objects of the definition—those defining occurrences. All of these are described as being things that we observe through direct perception. And this is done in the context of the direct form of accurate perception, as it is identified within the division of accurate perception into four different types. As such, we can say further that it is not refering to the way in which omniscience itself perceives objects directly.

rows.english: And so we can say that the states of mind that focus upon these two—the typical expressions and the general archetypes—take on an aspect of the same two. And that aspect itself is the manifest object of those states of mind. Which means that we can describe both the objects here, and the states of mind holding those objects, as being direct, or manifest. And what we say is that the word “direct” here is being applied to the object involved directly; and to the subject involved in only a nominal way.

rows.english: As such, we can say even with things like the two forms of the tendency to grasp to some self-nature of things that the appearance of two “selfs” here is made directly. rows.wylie: de ltar na de kho na nyid kyi don gtan la phab pa goms pa las, rnal 'byor pa 'phags pa'i lam mngon sum du mdzad pa'i mnyam gzhag gis snang ba'i spros pa ma gzigs pa'i tshul gyis de kho na nyid gzigs pa de dag la chos gang la yang bden par mngon par zhen pa'i rtog pa thog ma med pa nas goms pa rnams ldog par 'gyur te
rows.english: And so it is that when they have accustomed ourselves to establishing just what it is that suchness refers to, the deep practitioner is able to go into a balanced meditation where they can manifest—directly—the path of a realized being. And then this meditation helps them to see suchness, in the manner of not seeing the various ways that things might appear to one as false elaborations. Thus then are such people able to put a stop to any habit of the kind that we have possessed for time with no beginning, of a notion where they feel strongly attached to the idea that any object at all could exist in truth.

rows.acip: 'O NA PHUNG PO BDAG TU MI 'DOD PA'I LUGS LA YANG, GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED MNGON SUM DU MTHONG BA'I TSE, BDAG GI MTSAN GZHIR 'JOG PA'I GANG ZAG THAMS CAD MED PAR MTHONG DGOS PAR 'GYUR TE, RGYU MTSAN MTSUNGS PA'I PHYIR RO ZHE NA,

rows.english: One may come then with the following question: Even according to the system where they disagree that the parts to the person are the self, something is supposed to happen when you see, directly, the fact that there is no self-nature to the person. rows.acip: GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED PA MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PAR 'DOD PA'I TSE NA, RTAG PA'I BDAG TZAM ZHIG SPONG BA STE MED PAR MTHONG ZHING, RTAG PA'I BDAG 'DI NI 'JIG LTA LHAN SKYES KYI NGAR 'DZIN GYI RTEN TE DMIGS PA DANG RNAM PA GANG GI YUL DU'ANG MI 'DOD PA,
rows.wylie: gang zag gi bdag med pa mngon sum du rtogs par 'dod pa'i tshe na, rtag pa'i bdag tsam zhig spong ba ste med par mthong zhing, rtag pa'i bdag 'di ni 'jig lta lhan skyes kyi ngar 'dzin gyi rten te dmigs pa dang rnam pa gang gi yul du'ang mi 'dod pa
rows.english: Now suppose we are talking about the point where one is desirous of perceiving the lack of self to the person, in a direct way. Here the only thing we have to eliminate is the self which is unchanging; which is to say, we have to see that it is something which does not exist. And yet neither do we accept that this unchanging self is the basis for the innate form of the view of destruction: our grasping to a “me.” That is, we do not accept that it is the object here, whether you're talking about that thing which we are focused upon, or the aspect which this focus takes.

rows.acip: 'DI NI KHYOD KYIS DBU MA'I BSTAN BCOS KYI DGONGS PA MA RIG PA ZHIG STE, 'DI'I DGONGS PA NI GAL TE MIG LA SOGS PA RNAMS KYI RANG GI NGO BO RTEN CING 'BREL PAR 'BYUNG BA BYIS PA'I SKYE BOS GZUNG BAR BYA BA GANG YIN PA 'DI NYID MIG LA SOGS PA DE RNAMS KYI RANG BZHIN YIN LUGS YIN NA NI, RANG BZHIN DE PHYIN CI LOG GI BLOS KYANG MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA'I PHYIR, TSANGS PAR SPYOD PA DON MED PAR 'GYUR NA,
rows.wylie: 'di ni khyod kyis dbu ma'i bstan bcos kyi dgongs pa ma rig pa zhig ste, 'di'i dgongs pa ni gal te mig la sogs pa rnams kyi rang gi ngo bo rten cing 'brel par 'byung ba byis pa'i skye bos gzung bar bya ba gang yin pa 'di nyid mig la sogs pa de rnams kyi rang bzhin yin lugs yin na ni, rang bzhin de phyin ci log gi blos kyang mngon sum du rtogs pa'i phyir, tshangs par spyod pa don med par 'gyur na
rows.english: But with this, the fact is that you are showing how you fail to understand the true intent of the classical commentary on the middle way. What this is actually trying to say is that—suppose the essential nature of the eye and so on is that they occur through a process of dependence. And suppose that people who are still infants hold to this idea. If this by itself were the ultimate nature or way of being for the eye and so forth, then it would be the case that even a mistaken state of mind could perceive this nature directly. And then living the entire life of purity would be pointless.

rows.acip: RNAM PA KUN MKHYEN PA NYID KYI YE SHES NI, SHES BYA THAMS CAD MNGON SUM DU MKHYEN PA'I MTSAN NYID CAN DU 'DOD DE, RNAM MKHYEN DE LAS GZHAN PA'I SHES PA THAMS CAD NI YUL NYI TSE BA TZAM LA 'JUG PA NYID KYIS, SHES BYA THAMS CAD MNGON SUM DU MKHYEN PA ZHES BYA BAR MI 'DOD DO,,
rows.wylie: rnam pa kun mkhyen pa nyid kyi ye shes ni, shes bya thams cad mngon sum du mkhyen pa'i mtshan nyid can du 'dod de, rnam mkhyen de las gzhan pa'i shes pa thams cad ni yul nyi tshe ba tsam la 'jug pa nyid kyis, shes bya thams cad mngon sum du mkhyen pa zhes bya bar mi 'dod do
rows.english: The wisdom of omniscience itself is something that we hold to have an own quality of the direct perception of all knowable objects. All states of mind other than this omniscience are limited to engaging in their objects in only a partial way; as such, we would not refer to them as the direct knowledge of all existing entities.

rows.acip: SRID PA GSUM PO 'DI DAG MA LUS PA GDOD MA NAS RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA MED PAR MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA DE YANG NI, THA SNYAD PA KUN RDZOB BDEN PA'I STOBS KYIS TE KUN RDZOB TU 'GOG PAR 'GRO BA STE DE LA SNYOMS PAR 'JUG GO
rows.wylie: srid pa gsum po 'di dag ma lus pa gdod ma nas rang bzhin gyis skye ba med par mngon sum du rtogs pa de yang ni, tha snyad pa kun rdzob bden pa'i stobs kyis te kun rdzob tu 'gog par 'gro ba ste de la snyoms par 'jug go
rows.english: And so suppose that we are able to realize, directly, that there is nothing about the entirety of these three realms of existence which has ever started through any nature of its own: and it has been this way since time with no beginning. And in this case, we have—through the power of nominal, or deceptive reality—come to the point where things are stopped, in a nominal sense. And then we go into a balanced meditation on this very point.

rows.acip: DE SKAD DU SA BCU PA LAS, KYE RGYAL BA'I SRAS DAG BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA'I SA DRUG PA YAN CHAD, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA'I 'GOG PA LA SNYOMS PAR 'JUG PA STE, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA'I SA BDUN PA 'DI LA GNAS PA'I BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' NI, SEMS KYI SKAD CIG SEMS KYI SKAD CIG LA YANG 'GOG PA LA SNYOMS PAR 'JUG CING LDANG STE, 'GOG PA MNGON SUM DU BYAS ZHES NI MI BYA'O ZHES RGYAS PAR GSUNGS SO,,
rows.wylie: de skad du sa bcu pa las, kye rgyal ba'i sras dag byang chub sems dpa'i sa drug pa yan chad, byang chub sems dpa'i 'gog pa la snyoms par 'jug pa ste, byang chub sems dpa'i sa bdun pa 'di la gnas pa'i byang chub sems dpa' ni, sems kyi skad cig sems kyi skad cig la yang 'gog pa la snyoms par 'jug cing ldang ste, 'gog pa mngon sum du byas zhes ni mi bya'o zhes rgyas par gsungs so
rows.english: We see this described, in some detail, in The Sutra on the Ten Levels: O children of the Victors, beyond the sixth level of the bodhisattva, one goes into a balanced meditation upon the cessation of a bodhisattva. That is, a bodhisattva who is staying at the seventh bodhisattva level enters into balanced meditation upon—and then arises from—their cessation, moment by mental moment. We do not though refer to this as having gone directly into the cessation.

rows.acip: CHOS NYID MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA'I MI RTOG YE SHES NYAN RANG GIS KYANG 'THOB PAR GSUNGS PAS, DE KHO NA NYID KYI RTOGS PA YOD NA TSOGS GZHAN GSOG PA LA 'BAD PA MI DGOS KYI, DE NYID LA GOMS PAS CHOG GO ZHES PA NI MI MKHAS PA'I BAB COL DU SMRA BA'O,,
rows.wylie: chos nyid mngon sum du rtogs pa'i mi rtog ye shes nyan rang gis kyang 'thob par gsungs pas, de kho na nyid kyi rtogs pa yod na tshogs gzhan gsog pa la 'bad pa mi dgos kyi, de nyid la goms pas chog go zhes pa ni mi mkhas pa'i bab col du smra ba'o
rows.english: So too, it has been stated that listeners and self-made buddhas can also attain that wisdom, beyond imagining any self-existence, with which one realizes—directly—the true nature of things. As such, it is the ravings of a person who has no mastery when someone comes and says that—if you have reached the realization of suchness—then there is no need for you to make efforts in accumulating any other collections of good deeds; and that it will then be enough for you just to get used to this very thing. Finishing off negative emotions

rows.acip: BDEN 'DZIN GYI BAG CHAGS MA LUS PA ZAD DE SANGS RGYAS PA NAS DUS RTAG TU DON DAM BDEN PA MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA'I MNYAM GZHAG LA BZHUGS PAS, DE LAS BZHENGS PA'I MNYAM RJES RES 'JOG MED PA'I PHYIR DANG,
rows.wylie: bden 'dzin gyi bag chags ma lus pa zad de sangs rgyas pa nas dus rtag tu don dam bden pa mngon sum du rtogs pa'i mnyam gzhag la bzhugs pas, de las bzhengs pa'i mnyam rjes res 'jog med pa'i phyir dang
rows.english: Then comes a point when we are able to finish off all of the deep seeds for the tendency to hold things as being real, and reach our own enlightenment. From this time on, we are forever in a deep meditation where we are perceiving, directly, ultimate reality. As such, we no longer engage in a successive state, in the sense of first being in deep meditation and then coming out into what is termed the “aftermath” of that meditation.

rows.acip: ZHES SANGS RGYAS KYIS SNANG BA JI SNYED PA THAMS CAD MNGON SUM DU MKHYEN PA DANG, YANG GNYIS SU SNANG BA'I TSUL GYIS SHES PA DANG SHES BYA GANG YANG MI MTHONG BAR GSUNGS PA DANG,
rows.wylie: zhes sangs rgyas kyis snang ba ji snyed pa thams cad mngon sum du mkhyen pa dang, yang gnyis su snang ba'i tshul gyis shes pa dang shes bya gang yang mi mthong bar gsungs pa dang
rows.english: What this is saying is that an Enlightened Being knows, directly, the total amount of things that ever appear. At the same time though, they see nothing—neither knowing nor what is known—in a manner where these appear in a dualistic way.

rows.acip: CHEN PO GZHAN DAG GIS KYANG DE DANG 'DRA BAR GSUNGS PA RNAMS LA, SHES PA DANG SHES BYA GANG YANG MI MTHONG BA SANGS RGYAS RANG SNANG GI DBANG DU BYAS SHING, SHES BYA THAMS CAD MNGON SUM DU GZIGS PA GDUL BYA GZHAN SNANG GI MKHYEN TSUL YIN PAS,
rows.wylie: chen po gzhan dag gis kyang de dang 'dra bar gsungs pa rnams la, shes pa dang shes bya gang yang mi mthong ba sangs rgyas rang snang gi dbang du byas shing, shes bya thams cad mngon sum du gzigs pa gdul bya gzhan snang gi mkhyen tshul yin pas
rows.english: Other great thinkers too have made the same sort of statements; and then we can say about these pronouncements that not seeing any state of mind, or anything known, at all relates to how things appear to the Buddha themselves; and then being able to see all existing entities directly relates to the way in which this being sees things appearing as something other to disciples.

rows.english: Due to the fact that they have sprung up, an impression with a wrong way of looking at things springs up, and some things seem as though they are pleasant from their own side, and other things seem as though they are unpleasant from their own side. Due to the fact that this impression has sprung up, the emotion of liking springs up, where you focus on a pleasant object and don't want to lose it. And the emotion of disliking springs up, where you focus on an unpleasant object and want to avoid it. This then forces you to collect karma. And karma forces you to spin around in the wheel of suffering life. And this is why the Buddhas have said that this suffering life is something forced on us because we have not been able to see, directly, the essence of the Ones Gone Thus [that is, emptiness].

rows.english: Consider now bodhisattvas who have reached one of the pure levels. Even though objects appear to their minds, during what we call the "subsequent period," as something which exists truly, they have no belief in them this way. And this is because neither situation applies to realized beings who are not yet Buddhas and whoare perceiving the real nature of things directly; that is, physical matter and other objects do not appear to them as if they existed truly, and they do not believe that these objects exist that way.

rows.acip: 'O NA RANG LUGS LA SGRIB GNYIS KYI DRI MA SPONG TSUL JI LTAR BYED SNYAM NA BDAG MED, PHRA RAGS GSUM RIM PA BZHIN DU THOS BSAM GYIS GTAN LA PHAB NAS SGOM BYUNG GIS BSGOMS PAS MNGON SUM DU MTHONG BA NA NYON MONGS PA'I SGRIB PA DANG SHES SGRIB, RAGS PA DANG SHES SGRIB PHRA MO GSUM RTZA BA NAS ZAD PAR BYED NUS ZHES STON PA YIN, PAS DNGOS SMRA BA 'DOD PA LTAR DRI MA BDEN GRUB KHAS BLANGS NAS SPONG BA MIN GYI DRI MA BDEN MED BSGOMS NAS DRI MA SPONG BA YIN NO ZHES RANG LUGS KYI SGRIB GNYIS SPONG TSUL GTZO BOR STON PA YIN
rows.wylie: 'o na rang lugs la sgrib gnyis kyi dri ma spong tshul ji ltar byed snyam na bdag med, phra rags gsum rim pa bzhin du thos bsam gyis gtan la phab nas sgom byung gis bsgoms pas mngon sum du mthong ba na nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa dang shes sgrib, rags pa dang shes sgrib phra mo gsum rtsa ba nas zad par byed nus zhes ston pa yin, pas dngos smra ba 'dod pa ltar dri ma bden grub khas blangs nas spong ba min gyi dri ma bden med bsgoms nas dri ma spong ba yin no zhes rang lugs kyi sgrib gnyis spong tshul gtso bor ston pa yin
rows.english: "Well then," you may think to yourself, "how do we in our own position describe the process by which one eliminates the various impurities?" It has been taught that: One can gain the ability toput a total end tothe three—that is, to the obstacles of the mental afflictions, to the gross obstacles to omniscience, and to the subtle obstacles to omniscience—if one meditates with that wisdom which grows from meditation and which sees directly the three degrees of the lack of a self-nature; this itself grows from following the practices of study and meditation to come to an understanding of these three. Given this statement, it is not the case that in our own position we believe—as do those who assert the existence of functional things which exist truly—that one can eliminate impurities that one asserts exist in truth. The citation rather is demonstrating the principal tenet of how our own system describes the process of eliminating the two obstacles; that is, that we eliminate impurities by meditating upon how these same impurities lack any true existence. The next selection introduces, briefly, the concept of the three levels of deep practice that correlate to the three degrees of selflessness. It is taken from The "Cloud of Offerings, which Pleases the Wise, and Illuminates the True Thought of the Treatise known as the 'Ornament of Realizations,'" being a Combined Word Commentary and Dialectical Analysis of the Fifth Chapter of the Treatise, by Choney Lama Drakpa Shedrup (1675-1748), also an illustrious author of textbooks for Sera Mey Tibetan Monastery (ACIP electronic text S0195, Part Five, ff. 11b-12a).

rows.english: The point is that—when this state of mind is in the direct realization of emptiness—it sees what it sees in a way where the discrepancy has subsided. rows.english: Many different positions are taken in this regard. Some say that the actual perfection of wisdom is equivalent to the wisdom, in the mind of a person on the greater way, with which they realize emptiness. Others describe it as the wisdom, in this same person's mind, with which they see emptiness directly—and there are other descriptions as well. At any rate, they are all the same in saying that emptiness must be seen.

rows.english: We should say a little about this expression, the “great mastery of things that never grow.” This refers to a point at which one has eliminated the negative emotions, and achieved total mastery, fluency, in meditating upon non-conceptual wisdom, which perceives directly each and every instance of the very nature of all things, their emptiness of any natural existence. As such, all caused objects appear to this person exclusively in the nature of an illusion, as empty of any true existence, not only during periods of deep meditation but during the times between these meditations as well.

rows.acip: BZOD PA DE GSUM GANG RUNG THOB PA LA 'DUS BYAS KYI CHOS RNAMS RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA MED PAR RTOGS DGOS PA'I PHYIR STONG NYID NGES PAR RTOGS DGOS LA, 'BRING DANG CHEN PO LA NI STONG NYID MNGON SUM DU RTOGS DGOS SHING, CHEN PO LA NI NYON MONGS YANG SPANGS DGOS SO,,
rows.wylie: bzod pa de gsum gang rung thob pa la 'dus byas kyi chos rnams rang bzhin gyis skye ba med par rtogs dgos pa'i phyir stong nyid nges par rtogs dgos la, 'bring dang chen po la ni stong nyid mngon sum du rtogs dgos shing, chen po la ni nyon mongs yang spangs dgos so
rows.english: Whichever of these three types of mastery we attain, we must first come to the realization that no produced thing ever begins through any nature of its own—which is to say, we must definitely perceive emptiness. For the medium and greater forms of the mastery, this emptiness must be perceived directly; and for the greater form we must in addition eliminate our negative emotions.

rows.english: Generally speaking, the five different types of eyes have differing capacities of seeing things, either more or less widely. In this section though we can relate them to the eyes that a Buddha possesses. Their eyes of flesh then would see, directly, all of the grosser and more subtle forms that existed in the entire world.

rows.wylie: 'dir de kho na nyid kyi don mi shes pa'i so skye la byis pa'i ming gis btags pa ste 'phags pas ni chos kyi de kho na nyid mngon sum du gzigs pas byis pa zhes mi bya bar mkhas pa zhes bya la, de lta bu'i so skye rnams kyis de ltar mi shes pa'i phyir byis pa dang 'dra bas de'i ming gis brjod pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: Here we are applying the name of “child” to a common being: meaning one who still doesn't understand the meaning of suchness. Realized beings, on the other hand, have seen directly the suchness of things, and so we do not speak of them as “children,” but rather as “sages.” Common people like these are called “children” because they are similar to children, in the sense that they still don't have this understanding.

rows.acip: GZUGS SOGS KUN RDZOB PA'I CHOS GANG YIN YANG MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA DE'I TSE SPROS BCAS KYI RNAM PA SHAR BA'I TSUL GYIS RTOGS DGOS LA,
rows.wylie: gzugs sogs kun rdzob pa'i chos gang yin yang mngon sum du rtogs pa de'i tshe spros bcas kyi rnam pa shar ba'i tshul gyis rtogs dgos la
rows.english: You can take any deceptive object at all—be it something that we see with our eyes, or anything else—and say that when we perceive it directly we must be perceiving it in a way where it is exhibiting itself through some elaboration.

rows.acip: DE DAG GI CHOS NYID DON DAM PA'I CHOS GANG MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA DE'I TSE SPROS PA RNAM PAR BCAD PA'I TSUL GYIS RTOGS DGOS TE, BDEN GNYIS SO SO'I MTHONG TSUL GYI KHYAD PAR 'DI NI RTOGS PAR DKA' BA'I GNAS SO,,
rows.wylie: de dag gi chos nyid don dam pa'i chos gang mngon sum du rtogs pa de'i tshe spros pa rnam par bcad pa'i tshul gyis rtogs dgos te, bden gnyis so so'i mthong tshul gyi khyad par 'di ni rtogs par dka' ba'i gnas so
rows.english: And when we perceive, directly, the true nature of such objects—when we see any such ultimate object—then we must do so in a way where we are eliminating any elaborated appearance attached to them. This distinction in the way that we see each of the two realities is a point which is difficult to understand.

rows.acip: DER MA ZAD, CHOS GANG YIN YANG DE BDEN MED DU MNGON SUM DU MA RTOGS KYANG, DON SPYI'I TSUL GYIS RTOGS PA'I BLO DE'I SNANG NGOR SPROS PA 'CHAR YANG NGES NGOR SPROS PA GCOD DGOS SO,,
rows.wylie: der ma zad, chos gang yin yang de bden med du mngon sum du ma rtogs kyang, don spyi'i tshul gyis rtogs pa'i blo de'i snang ngor spros pa 'char yang nges ngor spros pa gcod dgos so
rows.english: But it doesn't stop here. Suppose, with reference to any object there may be, that—even if we do not perceive directly the fact that it has no reality—we perceive this fact in a way which utilizes mental images. Elaborations may be presenting themselves to this state of mind, but we must nonetheless stop any tendency we may have of actually perceiving them as they do.

rows.wylie: byang chub sems dpa' gang gis chos kyi rnam grangs sher phyin gyi gzhung 'di la brten nas bdag med pa'i don mngon sum du rtogs shing, don dam par skye ba med pa ste mi skye ba'i chos la bzod pa chen po thob na, gang zag de nyid kyis bzod pa thob pa'i gzhi de las bsod nams kyi phung po ches grangs med dpag tu med pa bskyed par 'gyur ro
rows.english: But any particular bodhisattva who is able to use this particular presentation of the Dharma, this classic of the perfection of wisdom—to perceive, directly, that object which is the lack of a self-nature to anything—thus gains great mastery towards the fact that, ultimately speaking, no object in the universe has any self-nature, nor ever begins. And then this same person creates mountains of merit, from the foundation of what they achieved mastery over, that are infinitely beyond all estimation.

rows.acip: STONG NYID MNGON SUM DU GZIGS PA'I SGO NAS YIN LA, THA SNYAD DU 'BYON BZHUD SOGS YOD KYANG, CHOS SKU STONG PA NYID KYI DBANG DU BYAS NA NI, 'BYON BZHUD SOGS DON DAM PAR MED DE, 'PHAGS PA BRGYAD STONG PA'I RTAG TU NGUS CHOS 'PHAGS BSTEN PA'I SKOR NAS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA 'BYON BZHUD SOGS JI LTAR YIN PA,
rows.wylie: stong nyid mngon sum du gzigs pa'i sgo nas yin la, tha snyad du 'byon bzhud sogs yod kyang, chos sku stong pa nyid kyi dbang du byas na ni, 'byon bzhud sogs don dam par med de, 'phags pa brgyad stong pa'i rtag tu ngus chos 'phags bsten pa'i skor nas de bzhin gshegs pa 'byon bzhud sogs ji ltar yin pa
rows.english: All this is in reference to their seeing emptiness directly. And although it is true that—in a nominal sense—there do exist actions like coming and going and the rest; nonetheless, relative to the reality body, to emptiness, there is no such thing as coming or going in an ultimate sense. This is all similar to the way for example that the coming and going of the One Gone Thus are explained in that section in the exalted scripture of the 8,000 Verses where the bodhisattva Sada Prarudita, Ever-Weeping, studied at the feet of Dharmodgata.

rows.english: On the subject of who it is that realizes, there are those-such as the high being Shariputra-who had not familiarized themselves in a very powerful way with emptiness during their present lifetime, but who had nonetheless become very acquainted with it in past lives. Those are minds which understand emptiness; which is to say that they do so directly, by means of wisdom.

rows.english: We deny that problems and their antidotes could exist in reality. But the great books-such as Entering the Middle Way, and its various commentaries-all agree that to eliminate negative seeds we need to see, directly, the fact that nothing is itself. And they agree that the realization of this reality is something that changes from instant to instant.

rows.english: It certainly is correct to say that a person can bring about their nirvana, in a case where nothing has any nature of its own; Because the following is true, when we are talking about that point in time where-because they have been accustoming themselves to the realization that nothing has any nature of its own-a person has reached a nirvana where something is still left over, and come to the end of each & every negative emotion. That is, at this point they have attained nirvana as something experienced in this very life; and they have done those things that they needed to do, as far as their keeping a pure way of life; and undertaking the necessary activities; and practicing the powers and so on.

rows.english: Let's consider all these things that are impermanent, and things which deceive us. Those beings who are wise ones, who have come to the end of everything they ever needed to accomplish-which is to say, those realized beings-see, directly, that these things are devoid of each & every kind of self-nature. rows.wylie: 'jug pa las, don dam sems bskyed rgyud la ma skyes na don dam pa'i byang chub sems dpa' zhes mi bya bar gsungs pa ni stong nyid mngon sum du rtogs ma myong na don dam pa'i byang chub sems dpa' zhes mi bya ba'i don yin la
rows.english: Entering the Middle Way says that if a person has yet to develop the ultimate form of the Wish for enlightenment in their mind, then they cannot be referred to as an "ultimate bodhisattva." What this is saying is that—if a person has yet to experience the direct perception of emptiness—then they cannot be called an "ultimate bodhisattva."[61]

rows.acip: ZHES SBYIN PA'I 'KHOR GSUM BDEN MED DU MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA'I SHES RAB ZIN PA'I SBYIN PA DE 'JIG RTEN LAS 'DAS PA'I SBYIN PA'I PHAR PHYIN DANG, DES MA ZIN PA'I SBYIN PA 'JIG RTEN PA'I PHAR PHYIN DU BSHAD DE,

rows.english: What this is saying is that it is a perfection of giving which is beyond the normal world whenever someone does their giving under the influence of that state of wisdom in which they have perceived, directly, that none of the three spheres in the act of giving has any truth of its own. And it is a perfection that belongs to the normal world if they perform their giving without being under this influence.

rows.acip: RGYU MTSAN DE CI'I SLAD DU ZHE NA, 'PHAGS PA'I GANG ZAG RNAMS NI CHOS THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN GYIS STONG PA 'DUS MA BYAS KYI CHOS NYID MNGON SUM DU RTOGS MYONG BAS RAB TU PHYE BA STE BZHAG PA'I SLAD DU'O ZHES ZHUS SO, ,'DI DAG NI 'PHAGS PA'I MNYAM GZHAG YE SHES KYI GZIGS NGOR SPROS PA DANG BRAL BA LA DGONGS SO,,
rows.wylie: rgyu mtshan de ci'i slad du zhe na, 'phags pa'i gang zag rnams ni chos thams cad rang bzhin gyis stong pa 'dus ma byas kyi chos nyid mngon sum du rtogs myong bas rab tu phye ba ste bzhag pa'i slad du'o zhes zhus so, ,'di dag ni 'phags pa'i mnyam gzhag ye shes kyi gzigs ngor spros pa dang bral ba la dgongs so
rows.english: And why, for what reason, is that? Because people who are realized beings have undergone an experience of realizing, directly, that each and every object which exists is the unproduced: that is, is something which is empty of having any nature of its own. Which is to say, they distinguish all these things—they establish them—with this experience. This is what Subhuti then respectfully speaks in reply. The actual point of this last part is to describe how the absence of elaboration—elaborating on things to where they seem to have some nature—makes its appearance to the perceptions of the meditative wisdom of a realized being.

rows.wylie: mi skye ba'i chos la bzod pa chen po thob pa ni, nyon mongs spangs shing chos thams cad rang bzhin gyis stong pa'i chos nyid mtha' dag mngon sum du rtogs pa'i mi rtog ye shes la goms pa dbang bsgyur thob pa'i phyir mnyam gzhag gi gnas skabs su ma zad , rjes thob kyi skabs su yang 'dus byas kyi chos thams cad bden stong sgyu ma lta bu 'ba' zhig tu snang bar 'gyur ro
rows.english: We should say a little about this expression, the "great mastery of things that never grow." This refers to a point at which one has eliminated the negative emotions, and achieved total mastery, fluency, in meditating upon non-conceptual wisdom, which perceives directly each and every instance of the very nature of all things, their emptiness of any natural existence. As such, all caused objects appear to this person exclusively in the nature of an illusion, as empty of any true existence, not only during periods of deep meditation but during the times between these meditations as well.

rows.wylie: mi skye ba'i chos la bzod pa thob pas chos thams cad bden med du mngon sum du gzigs shing gang lung bstan pa dang thob par bya ba dang 'tshang rgya bar 'gyur ba thams cad kyang rang bzhin gyis stong par gzigs pas, mar me mdzad las bden grub kyi chos gang yang blangs snyam du zhen pa med do
rows.english: When one reaches the stage of the great mastery of things that never grow, one directly perceives that no object at all has any true existence. One perceives that what was predicted to finally happen, and the thing one is to achieve, and becoming enlightened—all of them—are empty of any natural existence. As such the Buddha had no belief that he was taking up any truly existing Dharma at all from the Buddha, Light Maker.

rows.english: MING GIS BRJOD PA'I PHYIR RO,,Here we are applying the name of "child" to a common being: meaning one who still doesn't understand the meaning of suchness. Realized beings, on the other hand, have seen directly the suchness of things, and so we do not speak of them as "children," but rather as "sages." Common people like these are called "children" because they are similar to children, in the sense that they still don't have this understanding.[531]

rows.english: SO,,And when we perceive, directly, the true nature of such objects—when we see any such ultimate object—then we must do so in a way where we are eliminating any elaborated appearance attached to them. This distinction in the way that we see each of the two realities is a point which is difficult to understand.[558]

rows.english: Suppose, with reference to any object there may be, that—even if we do not perceive directly the fact that it has no reality—we perceive this fact in a way which utilizes mental images. Elaborations may be presenting themselves to this state of mind, but we must nonetheless stop any tendency we may have of actually perceiving them as they do.[559]

rows.english: bodhisattva who is able to use this particular presentation of the Dharma, this classic of the perfection of wisdom—to perceive, directly, that object which is the lack of a self-nature to anything—thus gains great mastery towards the fact that, ultimately speaking, no object in the universe has any self-nature, nor ever begins. rows.english: JI LTAR YIN PA,All this is in reference to their seeing emptiness directly. And although it is true that—in a nominal sense—there do exist actions like coming and going and the rest; nonetheless, relative to the reality body, to emptiness, there is no such thing as coming or going in an ultimate sense. This is all similar to the way for example that the coming and going of the One Gone Thus are explained in that section in the exalted scripture of the 8,000 Verses where the bodhisattva Sada Prarudita, Ever-Weeping, studied at the feet of Dharmodgata.[139][583]

rows.english: The Father and his spiritual Son came then first face-to-face on the soil of Chushar.  A great clamor burst forth from the sky, as if the gods were striking their mighty drums; and from the heavens as well the divine beings let loose a gentle shower of fragrant flower petals.  Everyone there saw these things, with their own eyes. * * * The Most Basic List of All Having completed the vows of refuge in the previous two classes, we continue our review of the foundation commitments with the very cornerstone of the individual liberation vows: the ten non-virtues that must be avoided by all Buddhist practitioners, at every level of their training.

rows.acip: RANG GIS STONG NYID MNGON SUM DU MA RTOGS KYANG , GZHAN LA STONG PA NYID BSTAN NAS, KHYOD KYI 'DI BSGOMS SHIG DANG , STONG PA NYID MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PAR 'GYUR BAS KHO BO DANG 'DRA BAR 'GYUR RO ZHES SMRAS PAS, PHA ROL GYIS DON GO NA LOG PA NYID SMRA BA'I RTZA LTUNG ,
rows.wylie: rang gis stong nyid mngon sum du ma rtogs kyang , gzhan la stong pa nyid bstan nas, khyod kyi 'di bsgoms shig dang , stong pa nyid mngon sum du rtogs par 'gyur bas kho bo dang 'dra bar 'gyur ro zhes smras pas, pha rol gyis don go na log pa nyid smra ba'i rtsa ltung
rows.english: (15) The root downfall of professing the complete opposite You commit this as follows.  In actuality, you have yet to perceive emptiness directly.  Nonetheless you teach the subject of emptiness to others and say, "Meditate as I have taught you, and you will come to see emptiness; then you'll be just like me."  The downfall is completed as soon as the other person grasps the meaning of your words. The Asian Classics Institute ____________________________________________________________________________ Diamond Mountain University Tantric Series Course II The Path to Bliss, Part Two Reading Ten: The Wish to Become the Angel * * * The Step that is the Place This brings us in The Path to Bliss to bodhichitta itself, the final of the seven steps in the cause-and-effect instructions for developing the Wish.  This is actually not a step towards the goal but the goal itself:  the last "effect" of the cause-and-effect progression.  His Holiness the First Panchen Lama very simply and clearly describes it here as the desire to become the Angel herself, so that we can be of real help to every living being.

rows.english: �And a completely enlightened being also possesses that high quality of their holy mind where they directly perceive every existing object in the universe:  meaning both the true nature of these objects and the total quantity of the objects, all at the same time. "They furthermore never stir from a state in which they are helping every living being to improve themselves:  they interact at every moment with each living being, without any sense of partiality, serving them with their great compassion, a love for each and every one which is like that of a mother for her only child.

rows.english: In those days he threw himself into the practice of that most profound of all things: the one thing that the Buddha really had in mind with everything he ever taught.  And the following thought came up within his holy mind: Suppose I were able to devote my heart entirely to that pair: to the emptiness yogas of balanced meditation and subsequent wisdom.  And suppose I were able to maintain these yogas over some period of time.  I don't see how it would be any difficult thing then to perceive emptiness directly.

rows.english: (Now the ritual with the eye ointment and spoon plants a mental seed for the initiate to give birth to extraordinary eyes in the form of the wisdom which perceives emptiness by means of mental images.  The mirror plants a seed for things to appear to us as an illusion, in the aftermath of the direct experience of emptiness.  And the bow and arrow plant a seed for us to perceive emptiness directly, without being obstructed by the medium of a mental image.) 88) Step Four: Grant permission to teach both the Dharma in general, and more specifically the secret teachings of the Five Families

rows.english: This fact is expressed in the text called Practicing in Secret: Have an actual consort And stay with them; Let the diamond rod And the lotus join; Come to the truth. Thus it is said, But suppose a person Who is just a beginner Gives up the practice Of an actual consort, And fails to meditate As it's described here. They will never be able To see that element Of enlightenment as It's taught so well, Trying to bring An approximation Through some other way. Those who are new To the practice should come To understand this fact, And come to knowledge In this way instead, With an immaculate Beginning, and middle, And end; there is No other way.

rows.english: It is the path of preparation here when we reach the state of special insight where we perceive emptiness.  We move up to the path of seeing then when we perceive emptiness directly.  The description of these and the other paths is thus the same as in the open teachings, the teachings of the perfections.

rows.acip: 'DI LA KHO NA RE, DE 'DRA BA'I MTSAN MED KYI RNAL 'BYOR DE SGOM STOBS KYIS STONG NYID MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA'I TSE YANG BZHIN LAG GI RNAM PA CAN GYI LHA'I SKU SNANG BAR THAL, KHYOD KYI DAM BCA' 'THAD PA'I PHYIR NA MA KHYAB STE, KUN RDZOB PA'I LHA'I SKU MI SNANG YANG RGYUD GYI SGO NAS LHA'I RNAL 'BYOR DU 'JOG PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: 'di la kho na re, de 'dra ba'i mtshan med kyi rnal 'byor de sgom stobs kyis stong nyid mngon sum du rtogs pa'i tshe yang bzhin lag gi rnam pa can gyi lha'i sku snang bar thal, khyod kyi dam bca' 'thad pa'i phyir na ma khyab ste, kun rdzob pa'i lha'i sku mi snang yang rgyud gyi sgo nas lha'i rnal 'byor du 'jog pa'i phyir
rows.english: At this point, someone might come and raise the following issue-- Suppose one does perform this deep practice where there are no more signs, as you've described it above, and then due to this meditation they manage to perceive emptiness directly.  Wouldn't the precious body of an Angel, complete with face and arms, be coming up in their mind at the very same time?  Because isn't your own position, in fact, correct? To this we answer, "It doesn't necessarily follow."  Because even though the precious body of an Angel which belongs to deceptive reality isn't in fact coming up in their mind at that point, we can still say that they are engaged in the deep practice of an Angel, as this practice is considered over a continuous length of time.

rows.wylie: de gnyis rang rang gi mtshan med kyi rnal 'byor du gyur pa'i stong nyid rtogs pa'i lhag mthong nas stong nyid mngon sum du ma rtogs tshun chad kyi lam rnams de gnyis rang rang gi sbyor lam yin pa sogs thams cad snga ma'i rigs 'gre sbyar nas shes par bya'o
rows.english: Consider next all the paths that occur within the period that begins with attaining extraordinary insight which perceives emptiness, and which represents a deep practice where there are no longer any signs, for the particular one of the two classes here; on up to the point where we are just about to see emptiness directly.  These paths together constitute the path of preparation for whichever one of the two classes here we are talking about. These and all the rest of the presentation for these two classes continues then to follow the same pattern as we had for the previous class.

rows.english: Someone may raise another point of this type: Isn't it necessarily the case that--in order to attain the actual clear light--one must necessarily attain the impure body of illusion first?  Because doesn't The Lantern say that "One must give birth to the body of illusion first, as a foundation for engaging directly in the clear light"? Our answer is that it doesn't necessarily follow.  And this is true because, in the path of the unsurpassed class, we do find explanations of how people who from the beginning belong to a fixed type travel the path.

rows.english: There is a part in Kedrup Je's Treatise on the Secret Teaching in Two Sections which presents this is a way which conflicts with the explanation above.  It says, Suppose now that the third of the empowerments is given in its actual form to a bodhisattva who is in his or her final rebirth.  This bodhisattva, through practice with their partner, is able to give birth to a form of ecstasy which is complete in every aspect.  They are though still maintaining--they have still not lost--their direct perception of emptiness from before.

rows.english: As such, when they receive the third empowerment in its actual form, their practice with their partner is done as a practice of mastering the life-wind. At the point of the fourth form of emptiness then, they come to perceive emptiness directly with the wisdom of ecstasy.

rows.acip: THEG PA GZHAN GYI BSKAL CHEN GRANGS MED GSUM GYI TSOGS GSOG PA'I DOD THUB PA'I SGYU LUS DANG , LHAN SKYES KYI BDE BAS DE KHO NA NYID MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA GNYIS NI LAM GZHAN LAS NUS MTHU CHES CHER LHAG PA'I RGYU MTSAN GYIS, THEG PA CHEN PO'I LAM GZHAN GYIS SPONG THEBS BDUN GYIS SPONG BAR GSUNGS PA'I LHAN SKYES KYI NYON MONGS RNAMS DON GYI 'OD GSAL MNYAM GZHAG THUN GCIG GIS SPONG NUS PAR 'DOD BZHIN DU, THEG PA CHEN PO'I LAM GZHAN GYIS SPONG THEBS BZHIS SPONG NUS PA'I SHES SGRIB LAM 'DIS SKOR DGUR PHYE NAS SPONG DGOS PAR 'DOD PA MI 'GRIG PA'I PHYIR RO,,
rows.wylie: theg pa gzhan gyi bskal chen grangs med gsum gyi tshogs gsog pa'i dod thub pa'i sgyu lus dang , lhan skyes kyi bde bas de kho na nyid mngon sum du rtogs pa gnyis ni lam gzhan las nus mthu ches cher lhag pa'i rgyu mtshan gyis, theg pa chen po'i lam gzhan gyis spong thebs bdun gyis spong bar gsungs pa'i lhan skyes kyi nyon mongs rnams don gyi 'od gsal mnyam gzhag thun gcig gis spong nus par 'dod bzhin du, theg pa chen po'i lam gzhan gyis spong thebs bzhis spong nus pa'i shes sgrib lam 'dis skor dgur phye nas spong dgos par 'dod pa mi 'grig pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: And this is true because it would be wrong to agree to the following idea. The body of illusion has the power to substitute for what the other ways describe as having to complete the collections over the length of three "countless" groups of great eons.  The pair of this body and the simultaneous bliss which perceives suchness directly are of infinitely greater power than other paths.  This fact provides the reason for the following position. It is agreed that with the actual clear light we can, in a single meditation session, eliminate the inborn mental afflictions which--it is said--we can eliminate with the other paths of the greater way only in seven passes.  It works the same way then with the obstacles to omniscience: those which can be eliminated with the other paths of the greater way only in four passes must be eliminated by this one path through breaking them out into nine different divisions.

rows.english: The eleventh downfall here is to refuse to accept--to have the wrong idea about--the immutable bliss, beyond any image that the world could offer, when it is given to you, because you doubt it, or are unsure about it.  The twelfth is when you criticize a pure being--a deep practitioner--directly, to their face.  You can get the details on these downfalls by referring to the explication on the root downfalls.

rows.acip: 'DI'I TSUL NI, SNGAR BZHIN KHAMS DKAR DMAR GYI THIG LE NYI KHRI CHIG STONG DRUG BRGYA DBU MA'I LAM NAS YAR MAR BRTZEGS PA LAS, MI 'GYUR BA'I BDE BA'I SKAD CIG MA NYI KHRI CHIG STONG DRUG BRGYA RIM PAR SKYE ZHING , DE RNAMS KYIS RIM BZHIN LAS RLUNG NYI KHRI CHIG STONG DRUG BRGYA DANG LUS KYI BEMS PO'I KHAMS NYI KHRI CHIG STONG DRUG BRGYA ZAD PAR BYAS TE, LUS STONG GZUGS RDO RJE'I SKU YAB YUM ZHAL SBYOR GYI RNAM PA CAN DANG SEMS CHOS THAMS CAD CIG CAR MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA'I MCHOG TU MI 'GYUR BA'I BDE BA CHEN PO'I NGO BOR GYUR PA'I KHA SBYOR YAN LAG BDUN LDAN GYI ZUNG 'JUG RDO RJE 'CHANG GI GONG 'PHANG MNGON DU BYAS TE,
rows.wylie: 'di'i tshul ni, sngar bzhin khams dkar dmar gyi thig le nyi khri chig stong drug brgya dbu ma'i lam nas yar mar brtsegs pa las, mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig ma nyi khri chig stong drug brgya rim par skye zhing , de rnams kyis rim bzhin las rlung nyi khri chig stong drug brgya dang lus kyi bems po'i khams nyi khri chig stong drug brgya zad par byas te, lus stong gzugs rdo rje'i sku yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can dang sems chos thams cad cig car mngon sum du rtogs pa'i mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po'i ngo bor gyur pa'i kha sbyor yan lag bdun ldan gyi zung 'jug rdo rje 'chang gi gong 'phang mngon du byas te
rows.english: Here is how this is done.  As before, we pile up 21,600 drops of the white and red element, moving up and down in the central channel.  With this we get the serial arisal of 21,600 moments of immutable bliss.  These then put an end to--one by one--21,600 different winds of deeds, as well as 21,600 material parts of the body.  And then we bring forth the state of the Keeper of the Diamond: the combination of the two, the seven-part joining, whose very nature is the highest form of great, immutable bliss that directly perceives, in every single instant, each and every living being and thing in the universe--a bliss that takes the aspect of the body of empty form, the diamond bodies of the Angel Man and Woman, joined in a kiss.

rows.english: The instruction was elucidated by Lord Naropa, a crowning jewel who stood above all the sages and saints of India, the Land of the Realized.  He himself received it as a personal teaching from the Holy One, when he met Her face to face.

rows.acip: RANG GI GA-YAS SU PHA, GA-YON DU MA, MDUN DU MNGON SUM DU GNOD PA'I DGRA, MI MNGON PAR GNOD PA'I 'DRE, DNGOS SU GNOD PA MI BYED KYANG DE LA BRTEN NAS BYUR KHA 'DREN PA STE DGRA 'DRE BYUR GSUM,
rows.wylie: rang gi ga-yas su pha, ga-yon du ma, mdun du mngon sum du gnod pa'i dgra, mi mngon par gnod pa'i 'dre, dngos su gnod pa mi byed kyang de la brten nas byur kha 'dren pa ste dgra 'dre byur gsum
rows.english: On my own right is my father, and my mother is on my left.  In front of me are a group that we call "enemy, spirit, and ill omens."  The enemies here are those who do me harm that I can see.  The spirits are beings who harm me in ways that I cannot see.  And the ill omens are represented by beings who--although they don't do me any direct harm--nonetheless tend to attract disasters to my door.

rows.acip: ZHES PA LTAR SEMS KYI CHOS NYID RANG SEMS LHAN CIG SKYES PA MNGON SUM DU MTHONG STE 'TSANG RGYA BA LA, TSOGS GSOG SGRIB SBYONG GI ZHING MCHOG TU GYUR PA BLA MA LA SANGS RGYAS DNGOS SU BLTA BA'I MOS GUS KYI SGO NAS BSAGS SBYANG RLABS BO CHER SHUGS DRAG LA RGYUN RING BAR 'BAD DGOS PA'I GNAD KYIS YIN,
rows.wylie: zhes pa ltar sems kyi chos nyid rang sems lhan cig skyes pa mngon sum du mthong ste 'tshang rgya ba la, tshogs gsog sgrib sbyong gi zhing mchog tu gyur pa bla ma la sangs rgyas dngos su blta ba'i mos gus kyi sgo nas bsags sbyang rlabs bo cher shugs drag la rgyun ring bar 'bad dgos pa'i gnad kyis yin
rows.english: Here seeing directly the true nature of the mind, the simultaneous nature of our own mind, and thus attaining enlightenment, depends upon our Lama, who is the highest object with which we can amass the great collection of virtue, and purify ourselves of our obstacles.  This is due to a key point, where we make fierce efforts, over a long period of time, to carry out our collection of good and our purification of wrong in a tremendously powerful way: by means of a deep feeling of love and reverence where we look upon our Lama as being the Buddha himself.

rows.english: Here seeing directly the true nature of the mind, the simultaneous nature of our own mind, and thus attaining enlightenment, depends upon our Lama, who is the highest object with which we can amass the great collection of virtue, and purify ourselves of our obstacles.  This is due to a key point, where we make fierce efforts, over a long period of time, to carry out our collection of good and our purification of wrong in a tremendously powerful way: by means of a deep feeling of love and reverence where we look upon our Lama as being the Buddha himself.

rows.acip: DE NI SHIN TU PHRA BA'I GNYUG SEMS MNGON DU GYUR PA'I SKABS KYI STONG NYID MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA LTA BU YUL SNANG CAN ZHIG 'CHAR BA 'BYUNG YANG STONG NYID MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA NI MIN TE, 'DI SBYANG GZHI YIN, SBYANG GZHI DE SBYONG TSUL 'DI NYID KYI SMON LAM LAS, YID 'ONG RGYAL YUM PHYI YI RNAL 'BYOR MA,
rows.wylie: de ni shin tu phra ba'i gnyug sems mngon du gyur pa'i skabs kyi stong nyid mngon sum du rtogs pa lta bu yul snang can zhig 'char ba 'byung yang stong nyid mngon sum du rtogs pa ni min te, 'di sbyang gzhi yin, sbyang gzhi de sbyong tshul 'di nyid kyi smon lam las, yid 'ong rgyal yum phyi yi rnal 'byor ma
rows.english: And what is it like?  At that point when the primal state of mind manifests itself within us, there appears to us a kind of luminosity, and this experience is somewhat similar to the direct perception of emptiness.  We are not though actually perceiving emptiness, for this experience is exactly what we seek to purify ourselves of.  Just how we purify ourselves of it is described in lines such as those found in the prayer of this very ritual, where it talks about "lovely outer Angels, Mothers of the Victors."

rows.acip: GSUM LA BSTIM NAS LAS RUNG DU BYIN GYIS BRLABS PAS, GSANG BA'I PHO NYA LHAN SKYES KYI BDE STONG MOS PA YID BYED KYIS BSGOM PA THA, STONG NYID DON SPYI'I TSUL GYIS RTOGS PA 'BRING , STONG NYID MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA MCHOG STE DE GSUM RIM GYIS RGYUD LA SKYED PAR BYED PAS NA PHO NYA GSUM BSRES ZHES BYA,
rows.wylie: gsum la bstim nas las rung du byin gyis brlabs pas, gsang ba'i pho nya lhan skyes kyi bde stong mos pa yid byed kyis bsgom pa tha, stong nyid don spyi'i tshul gyis rtogs pa 'bring , stong nyid mngon sum du rtogs pa mchog ste de gsum rim gyis rgyud la skyed par byed pas na pho nya gsum bsres zhes bya
rows.english: When the beings we have invited to us melt into these inner three, this grants us a blessing that makes us fit for sacred work.  And this causes the three secrett Messengers to come forth, one after the other, in the stream of our mind.  The first of these three is meditating upon bliss and emptiness only as one imagines them to be; this is the lesser inner Messenger.  The middling inner Messenger is realizing emptiness through a mental picture.  The highest inner Messenger is the direct perception of emptiness.  So you develop these three in your mind in stages, and this is what the expression "fusion of the three Messengers" refers to.

rows.acip: RKANG BRGYAD KYI BSTOD PA SUS BTON KYANG, DE'I RGYUD LA BCOM LDAN 'DAS DPAL HE RU KA RDO RJE PHAG MO DANG BCAS PA, MKHA' 'GRO MA, L'A MA, DUM SKYES MA, GZUGS CAN MA LA SOGS PA SNYING PO'I RNAL 'BYOR MA BCU GNYIS DANG, KHAndA KA P'A LA DANG, RAB GTUM MA LA SOGS TE 'KHOR LO GSUM GYI DPA' BO DANG DPA' MO NYI SHU RTZA BZHI PHO NYA BSAM GYIS MI KHYAB PA DANG BCAS PA MNGON SUM DU BZHUGS NAS BYIN GYIS BRLAB CING, DGYES SHING BRTZE BAR MDZAD PA DANG,
rows.wylie: rkang brgyad kyi bstod pa sus bton kyang, de'i rgyud la bcom ldan 'das dpal he ru ka rdo rje phag mo dang bcas pa, mkha' 'gro ma, lA ma, dum skyes ma, gzugs can ma la sogs pa snying po'i rnal 'byor ma bcu gnyis dang, khaNDa ka pA la dang, rab gtum ma la sogs te 'khor lo gsum gyi dpa' bo dang dpa' mo nyi shu rtsa bzhi pho nya bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang bcas pa mngon sum du bzhugs nas byin gyis brlab cing, dgyes shing brtse bar mdzad pa dang
rows.english: Anyone who recites the Eight Verses of Praise has a host of Holy Beings enter into the stream of his or her mind and leave Their blessings there into him or herin actual fact come the Conqueror, the glorious Heruka, along with the Diamond Sow; the twelve Angels of the heart, including the Lady of the Sky, the Lady of La, the Lady of Pieces, the Lady of Forms, and the rest; Khanda Kapala, the Lady of Horrible Wrath, and all the others in short, all the twenty-four man and woman Warriors of the three groups, along with a totally inconceivable number of Messengers.  They are all very pleased, and They are very much in love, with the one who pronounces the Praise.

rows.acip: RDO RJE 'CHANG GIS GSUNGS PA'I RGYUD TSIG 'DI DAG LA NGES PA BRTAN PO RNYED PAR BYAS NAS RGYUD 'DI NAS 'DI LTAR GSUNGS YOD SNYAM DU DRAN PA'I SGO NAS, RKANG BRGYAD KYI BSTOD PA 'DON DUS, DA NGA'I RGYUD LA DPA' BO MKHA' 'GRO THAMS CAD MNGON SUM DU PHEBS NAS BZHUGS YOD SNYAM DU DGA' SPRO CHER BSKYED,
rows.wylie: rdo rje 'chang gis gsungs pa'i rgyud tshig 'di dag la nges pa brtan po rnyed par byas nas rgyud 'di nas 'di ltar gsungs yod snyam du dran pa'i sgo nas, rkang brgyad kyi bstod pa 'don dus, da nga'i rgyud la dpa' bo mkha' 'gro thams cad mngon sum du phebs nas bzhugs yod snyam du dga' spro cher bskyed
rows.english: Therefore you must seek to find an unshakable certainty about these words, spoken by the Keeper of the Diamond himself in the secret texts.  Bring this thought up in your mind and keep it there: "This is what is supposed to happen, for this is what is spoken in the secret books."  Then, when you recite the Eight Verses of Praise, let yourself feel an intense emotion of joy: think to yourself, "Now each and every Warrior and his Angel has actually come and entered into the stream of my mind, and now They are really living there."

rows.english: Suppose too that in some place in the world there appear people of an evil kind, or of harmful behavior. For as the secret root text says again,

rows.acip: DE BZHIN DU MTHONG LAM THOB NA MNYAM GZHAG GI SKABS SU STONG NYID MNGON SUM DU RTOGS NAS YUL YUL CAN RO GCIG TU GYUR NAS RTOG PA THAMS CAD 'GAG CING RJES THOB LA RTOG MED LA GNAS MI NUS LA, DER MA ZAD SA BCU'I BYANG SEMS KYANG MNYAM GZHAG GI SKABS SU RTOG PA 'GAG KYANG RJES THOB LA GNAS MI NUS SHING,
rows.wylie: de bzhin du mthong lam thob na mnyam gzhag gi skabs su stong nyid mngon sum du rtogs nas yul yul can ro gcig tu gyur nas rtog pa thams cad 'gag cing rjes thob la rtog med la gnas mi nus la, der ma zad sa bcu'i byang sems kyang mnyam gzhag gi skabs su rtog pa 'gag kyang rjes thob la gnas mi nus shing
rows.english: In the same way, when you achieve the path of seeing during the direct perception of emptiness it is as if the subject of your mind and the emptiness which it perceives become of one taste, and all of your conceptual thoughts stop.  During the period which follows the direct perception however you are not able to stay in that non-conceptual state.  Not only that, but even a spiritual warrior of the tenth level whose conceptual thoughts stop during the direct perception of emptiness is not able to stay in that state during the period after this perception.

rows.acip: ZHES DPAL 'KHOR LO BDE MCHOG YAB YUM GYI LAM LA SPYOD PA'I RNAL 'BYOR PA DE GDOL PA DANG KLA KLO LA SOGS PA 'JIG RTEN NA RIGS NGAN PAR BYED PA ZHIG YIN KYANG , DE GANG DU BZHUGS PA'I SA PHYOGS DER DPAL 'KHOR LO SDOM PA DPA' BO DANG MKHA' 'GRO'I TSOGS DANG BCAS PA MNGON SUM DU BZHUGS NAS LUNG PA DE'I SNOD BCUD THAMS CAD BYIN GYIS RLOBS PAR GSUNGS PA DANG ,
rows.wylie: zhes dpal 'khor lo bde mchog yab yum gyi lam la spyod pa'i rnal 'byor pa de gdol pa dang kla klo la sogs pa 'jig rten na rigs ngan par byed pa zhig yin kyang , de gang du bzhugs pa'i sa phyogs der dpal 'khor lo sdom pa dpa' bo dang mkha' 'gro'i tshogs dang bcas pa mngon sum du bzhugs nas lung pa de'i snod bcud thams cad byin gyis rlobs par gsungs pa dang
rows.english: What these lines are saying is that the Angels of the glorious Union of the Spheres, Man and Woman--together with all Their many Warriors and Angels--will truly come and live in any place where someone who tries to follow this practice stays.  They will furthermore do so even if that person is of what the world considers a lowly birth: if they are born among butchers or uncouth barbarians, or anything of the like.  No matter where it is that such a person is staying, the glorious Union of Spheres will come and stay there, and thereby bless that place and all of the beings residing there.

rows.acip: DE NI GZHI LA 'CHI BA'I TSE DANG, LAM BSGOMS PA'I STOBS KYIS RLUNG DBU MAR THIMS PA'I SKABS SU MNGON SUM DU NYAMS SU MYONG ZHING, NYAMS SU MYONG BA DE'I NGO BO NI SPROS PA'I MTHA' THAMS CAD DANG BRAL BA, STONG NYID MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA LTA BU'I STONG SANG NGE BA'I YUL SNANG CAN,
rows.wylie: de ni gzhi la 'chi ba'i tshe dang, lam bsgoms pa'i stobs kyis rlung dbu mar thims pa'i skabs su mngon sum du nyams su myong zhing, nyams su myong ba de'i ngo bo ni spros pa'i mtha' thams cad dang bral ba, stong nyid mngon sum du rtogs pa lta bu'i stong sang nge ba'i yul snang can
rows.english: In our original condition, this state of mind is experienced directly at the hour of death, at the point when the winds dissolve into the central channel.  On the path, this state of mind is experienced directly through the power of our meditation, at the point when the winds dissolve into the central channel.  And for either of these, the essence of what we experience is something devoid of every extreme, devoid of any elaboration.  Just as in the direct perception of emptiness, the object which appears to this state of mind is sheer emptiness.

rows.acip: DE LTA NA YANG GNYUG SEMS DE TSUL MIN YID BYED SOGS KYI RKYEN GYIS CHAGS SOGS DRI MA DANG LHAN CIG GNAS PA'I TSE, RANG LA YOD BZHIN DU BYIS PA RNAMS LA MNGON SUM DU MI 'GYUR BA NI, CHAGS SOGS DRI MAS BSGRIBS NAS MA MTHONG BA YIN ZHING,
rows.wylie: de lta na yang gnyug sems de tshul min yid byed sogs kyi rkyen gyis chags sogs dri ma dang lhan cig gnas pa'i tshe, rang la yod bzhin du byis pa rnams la mngon sum du mi 'gyur ba ni, chags sogs dri mas bsgribs nas ma mthong ba yin zhing
rows.english: The primordial mind is pure like this, yet when--due to factors such as regarding things in the wrong way--it exists alongside those impurities such as our attachment, it is not perceived this way.  Even though it belongs to us, manifest and unchanging, as children we cannot see it, because it is obscured by the stench of our craving and the like.

Even though it belongs to us, manifest and unchanging, as children we cannot see it, because it is obscured by the stench of our craving and the like."}

rows.english: And even those who do behold the true face of the primordial mind directly are unable to express its real nature.  As it says in the secret Teaching of Hevajra: "It is born within us, it cannot be expressed to another, it is not found anywhere."

rows.acip: DE LTA BU'I SGO NAS YID DU 'ONG BA'I RGYAL YUM RJE BTZUN MA NYID GDUL BYA'I DON DU PHYI YI RNAL 'BYOR MA GSUM GYI RNAM PAR BSTAN PA RNAMS KYI RANG ZHAL MNGON SUM DU MTHONG NAS DE RNAMS DANG SNYOMS 'JUG GI RTZE DGAS ROL PAR SHOG CIG CES DANG,

rows.english: So first of all, we are praying that by practicing like this, we may come to see directly the very own face of the Woman of Buddhas, the Holy Lady herself.  May we behold the three aspects of this outside Angel, displayed solely for the purpose of us disciples, and then come to laugh and play in that highest bliss of deep meditation with them.

rows.acip: SNANG MCHED THOB GSUM GYI GNYIS SNANG RAGS PA NUB NAS THAMS CAD STONG PA 'OD GSAL GYI GNYUG SEMS LHAN CIG SKYES PA'I YE SHES STONG ZHING GSAL BA'I GSANG BA'I MKHA' SPYOD YUM GYI RANG ZHAL GZHI DUS SU JI LTAR YOD PA LTAR MNGON SUM DU MTHONG NAS BDE STONG GI RTZE DGA' LA ROL PAR SHOG CIG ,CES SMON PA STE DE LA BYIN GYIS YAS RLOB CES GSUNGS SHING,

rows.english: And due to this, the rough appearance of the self-existence of those three--appearance, spread, and attainment--fades away into utter emptiness, and we see directly the wisdom of the inborn, simultaneous; the primordial mind of clear light.  This is the secret Angel--that which has existed within us always, as our original condition--the very own face of the Wife in heaven.  And we are praying here, lastly, that we may thus laugh and play in this highest bliss of bliss and voidness, which is to say, "may we be granted limitless blessing for this."

rows.acip: DE LA GOMS PAS MA DAG PA'I SGYU MA'I SKUR DNGOS GNAS LA LDANG ZHING, DE YANG 'OD GSAL DU ZHUGS PA LAS LHAN CIG SKYES PA'I YE SHES KYIS CHOS NYID MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA'I DON GYI 'OD GSAL MNGON DU 'GYUR ZHING, DE NAS RIM GYIS SLOB PA DANG MI SLOB PA'I ZUNG 'JUG RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MA'I GO 'PHANG MNGON DU BYED PA YIN NO,,
rows.wylie: de la goms pas ma dag pa'i sgyu ma'i skur dngos gnas la ldang zhing, de yang 'od gsal du zhugs pa las lhan cig skyes pa'i ye shes kyis chos nyid mngon sum du rtogs pa'i don gyi 'od gsal mngon du 'gyur zhing, de nas rim gyis slob pa dang mi slob pa'i zung 'jug rdo rje rnal 'byor ma'i go 'phang mngon du byed pa yin no
rows.english: And as we become well-versed in this, we rise up into the actual impure body of illusion.  And then we perceive the true nature of things directly, with the wisdom of simultaneous bliss, by entering into clear light, which means that we enter into the actual clear light.  And after that, first we achieve the union of the two which still requires learning, and then the union of the two which requires no more learning--the state of the Angel of Diamond.

rows.english: When you perceive emptiness with simultaneous bliss by means of a mental image, which is the approximate clear light, this is the medium form.  And when you perceive emptiness directly with simultaneous bliss, which is the actual clear light, this is the highest form.

rows.acip: PHYI NANG GI THABS KYIS RTZA RLUNG THIG LE LAS RUNG DU SGRUB PA'I THABS JE BZANG LAS BDE BA CHEN PO'I YE SHES DANG, YE SHES DES STONG NYID MNGON SUM DU BYAS PA'I NGES DON GYI RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MA DON GYI LHAN SKYES BSKYED PA NI DON DAM 'OD GSAL GYI RDZOGS RIM DNGOS DANG,
rows.wylie: phyi nang gi thabs kyis rtsa rlung thig le las rung du sgrub pa'i thabs je bzang las bde ba chen po'i ye shes dang, ye shes des stong nyid mngon sum du byas pa'i nges don gyi rdo rje rnal 'byor ma don gyi lhan skyes bskyed pa ni don dam 'od gsal gyi rdzogs rim dngos dang
rows.english: Then we use inner and outer methods to hone our channels, winds, and drops.  And through this process of purification comes the wisdom of great bliss--that wisdom we then use to bring about the direct perception of emptiness.  This induces the actual simultaneous state--the real Angel of Diamond.  And that in fact is the real stage of completion--the part that relates to ultimate reality, or bringing on the clear light.

rows.acip: MTHAR RLUNG DBU MAR ZHUGS GNAS THIM GSUM BYAS PA LA BRTEN NAS MTSON BYED DPE'I 'OD GSAL DON SPYI'I TSUL GYIS SKYE LA, DE'I RGYUN BSKYANGS PAS MTSON BYA DON GYI 'OD GSAL MNGON SUM DU SKYE BA YIN PAS NA CHOS NYID BRGYUD NAS STON PA ZAB PA YIN LA,
rows.wylie: mthar rlung dbu mar zhugs gnas thim gsum byas pa la brten nas mtshon byed dpe'i 'od gsal don spyi'i tshul gyis skye la, de'i rgyun bskyangs pas mtshon bya don gyi 'od gsal mngon sum du skye ba yin pas na chos nyid brgyud nas ston pa zab pa yin la
rows.english: By the end of this process then they will manage to get the inner winds to enter, stay, and dissolve within the central channel.  Due to this they will be able to bring on, in a way that depends on a mental image of the thing, the approximate clear light--which is only a representation of the real thing.  As they continue a sustained practice of this clear light then it brings on the direct experience of the actual clear light: the real thing that was only being represented before.  And this then is what makes teaching the true nature of things through a medium so much more profound.

rows.english: Here when we talk about the "outer Heaven" we are referring to the paradise known as the "Heaven of Purity."  When we speak of the "inner Heaven," we mean the actual clear light, which is where the primal state of mind, our mind turned into the very nature of great bliss, perceives directly the fact that nothing has any nature of its own--that is, voidness.

rows.english: This fact is expressed in the text called Practicing in Secret: Have an actual partner And stay with them; Let the diamond rod And the lotus join; Come to the truth. Thus it is said, But suppose a person Who is just a beginner Gives up the practice Of an actual partner And fails to meditate As it's described here. rows.english: "How do we establish," one may ask, "that there exists a Keeper of the Diamond that we cannot see?"  The Keeper of the Diamond "lives His life within the body of our own spiritual Master," meaning that He assumes the form of our Master.  And since this Master accepts from us the outer and inner offerings, it is as if the Keeper of the Diamond has become someone we can see.

rows.english: "This would seem though to contradict Lord Milarepa's statement that 'Actual, physical spiritual partners are hard to find.' rows.english: There are different ways of explaining the first two lines of verse here, but we can start by saying that a certain subject state of mind--the wisdom of great, simultaneous bliss--is perceiving, in a direct way, the object of voidness. rows.wylie: rgyud bla ma rtsa 'grel gyi dgongs pa mthar thug yin te, bdag 'dzin gnyis kyi bag chags la brten nas de gnyis skyes, de la brten nas rang ngos nas grub pa'i yid 'ong ba dang yid mi 'ong du snang ba'i tshul min yid byed kyi rnam rtog skye, de la brten nas yid 'ong la dmigs nas mi 'bral bar 'dod pa'i 'dod chags dang , yid mi 'ong la dmigs nas 'bral 'dod kyi zhe sdang skyes, de'i dbang gis las bsags las de'i dbang gis 'khor bar 'khor ba dang de ltar 'khor ba de yang , de bzhin gshegs pa'i snying po mngon sum du ma rtogs pa'i dbang gis yin par gsungs pa'i phyir
rows.english: This then is the ultimate idea within the root text and the commentary of the Higher Line, [written by Maitreya and Asanga]: Due to the mental seeds for the two kinds of tendencies to grasp to some self- nature, these two tendencies themselves spring up. Due to the fact that they have sprung up, an impression with a wrong way of looking at things springs up, and some things seem as though they are pleasant from their own side, and other things seem as though they are unpleasant from their own side. Due to the fact that this impression has sprung up, the emotion of liking springs up, where you focus on a pleasant object and don't want to lose it. And the emotion of disliking springs up, where you focus on an unpleasant object and want to avoid it. This then forces you to collect karma. rows.wylie: dpe de bzhin du byang sems snying rje'i dbang du gyur pa rnams kyis kyang, sems can 'jig lta'i mtshor de rgyas pa'i phyir du 'bab pa'i ma rig pa'i chu sngon po rgya che ba dang ldan pa, tshul min yid byed kyi rnam rtog gi rlung gis bskyod pa'i nang na gnas pa, nam kha'i zla ba lta bu'i rang gi las dkar nag gi gzugs brnyan lta bur mdun na gnas pa rnams
rows.english: The metaphor holds with those bodhisattvas who are slaves to thoughts of compassion. They are focusing on living beings who possess vast rivers of ignorance, feeding into an ocean of the view of destruction, swelling it. These beings exist within waters which are stirred by the winds of their wrong ideas—of how they think of things in the wrong way. And there in front of them lies the reflection of how they have treated others—right or wrong—like that of the moon in the sky.

rows.english: Consider these same enemy destroyers. It is true that they have not yet realized, entirely, the fact that the person has no self nature. This is because they have yet to perceive directly the fact that the person has no nature. rows.english: This then is the ultimate idea within the root text and the commentary of the Higher Line, [written by Maitreya and Asanga]: Due to the mental seeds for the two kinds of tendencies to grasp to some self- nature, these two tendencies themselves spring up. Due to the fact that this impression has sprung up, the emotion of liking springs up, where you focus on a pleasant object and don't want to lose it. And the emotion of disliking springs up, where you focus on an unpleasant object and want to avoid it. This then forces you to collect karma. And karma forces you to spin around in the wheel of suffering life. rows.english: Here is the third point, [which is advice to those who seek to attain liberation, that it is therefore very right that they should meditate upon emptiness]. As such--that is, as we have just explained--the case is that all these attempts to overthrow those who accept the idea of emptiness are completely incorrect. They will also be disproved by the various kinds of reasoning which we will present later on. And so it is that even those who wish no more than to achieve the "enlightenment" which is the goal of the Listener and "Self-Made Buddha" tracks must still, beyond a shadow of a doubt, meditate upon emptiness, for the following reason. The tendency to hold things as existing truly is that form of ignorance, involved with mental affliction, which is the root of the circle of suffering. And it is completely impossible to attain freedom unless one can overthrow the existence of the object which this ignorance thinks it sees.

rows.acip: RGYUD BLA MA RTZA 'GREL GYI DGONGS PA MTHAR THUG YIN TE, BDAG 'DZIN GNYIS KYI BAG CHAGS LA BRTEN NAS DE GNYIS SKYES, DE LA BRTEN NAS RANG NGOS NAS GRUB PA'I YID 'ONG BA DANG YID MI 'ONG DU SNANG BA'I TSUL MIN YID BYED KYI RNAM RTOG SKYE, DE LA BRTEN NAS YID 'ONG LA DMIGS NAS MI 'BRAL BAR 'DOD PA'I 'DOD CHAGS DANG , YID MI 'ONG LA DMIGS NAS 'BRAL 'DOD KYI ZHE SDANG SKYES, DE'I DBANG GIS LAS BSAGS LAS DE'I DBANG GIS 'KHOR BAR 'KHOR BA DANG DE LTAR 'KHOR BA DE YANG , DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA'I SNYING PO MNGON SUM DU MA RTOGS PA'I DBANG GIS YIN PAR GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR
rows.wylie: rgyud bla ma rtsa 'grel gyi dgongs pa mthar thug yin te, bdag 'dzin gnyis kyi bag chags la brten nas de gnyis skyes, de la brten nas rang ngos nas grub pa'i yid 'ong ba dang yid mi 'ong du snang ba'i tshul min yid byed kyi rnam rtog skye, de la brten nas yid 'ong la dmigs nas mi 'bral bar 'dod pa'i 'dod chags dang , yid mi 'ong la dmigs nas 'bral 'dod kyi zhe sdang skyes, de'i dbang gis las bsags las de'i dbang gis 'khor bar 'khor ba dang de ltar 'khor ba de yang , de bzhin gshegs pa'i snying po mngon sum du ma rtogs pa'i dbang gis yin par gsungs pa'i phyir
rows.english: This then is the ultimate idea within the root text and the commentary of the Higher Line, [written by Maitreya and Asanga]: Due to the mental seeds for the two kinds of tendencies to grasp to some self- nature, these two tendencies themselves spring up. Due to the fact that they have sprung up, an impression with a wrong way of looking at things springs up, and some things seem as though they are pleasant from their own side, and other things seem as though they are unpleasant from their own side. Due to the fact that this impression has sprung up, the emotion of liking springs up, where you focus on a pleasant object and don't want to lose it. And the emotion of disliking springs up, where you focus on an unpleasant object and want to avoid it. This then forces you to collect karma. And karma forces you to spin around in the wheel of suffering life. And this is why the Buddhas have said that this suffering life is something forced on us because we have not been able to see, directly, the essence of the Ones Gone Thus [that is, emptiness]. *********

rows.english: This then is the ultimate idea within the root text and the commentary of the Higher Line, [written by Maitreya and Asanga]: Due to the mental seeds for the two kinds of tendencies to grasp to some self- nature, these two tendencies themselves spring up. Due to the fact that they have sprung up, an impression with a wrong way of looking at things springs up, and some things seem as though they are pleasant from their own side, and other things seem as though they are unpleasant from their own side. Due to the fact that this impression has sprung up, the emotion of liking springs up, where you focus on a pleasant object and don't want to lose it. And the emotion of disliking springs up, where you focus on an unpleasant object and want to avoid it. This then forces you to collect karma. And karma forces you to spin around in the wheel of suffering life. And this is why the Buddhas have said that this suffering life is something forced on us because we have not been able to see, directly, the essence of the Ones Gone Thus [that is, emptiness]. 29 The Glass of Liquid: Source of the Example
